scenes.dialogue: You file a civil suit. The judge says this plaint cannot proceed. Is it rejected, or returned? Each leads to a different procedure, and a different remedy.
The answer lies in Order Seven of the Code of Civil Procedure, or C P C, and four leading Supreme Court judgments.
scenes.shown: The answer lies in Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure, or CPC, and four leading Supreme Court judgments.

scenes.dialogue: Two rules, two questions. Rule Ten deals with return: is this the proper court? It commonly applies when territorial or pecuniary jurisdiction is missing.
scenes.shown: Two rules, two questions. Rule 10 deals with return: is this the proper court? It commonly applies when territorial or pecuniary jurisdiction is missing.

scenes.dialogue: Rule Eleven deals with rejection: does a statutory ground stop the plaint from proceeding? A weak case alone is not enough.
scenes.shown: Rule 11 deals with rejection: does a statutory ground stop the plaint from proceeding? A weak case alone is not enough.

scenes.dialogue: Which grounds count? Rule Eleven lists six. First, the plaint discloses no cause of action. Second, the relief is undervalued, and not corrected in the time fixed.
scenes.shown: Which grounds count? Rule 11 lists six. First, the plaint discloses no cause of action. Second, the relief is undervalued, and not corrected in the time fixed.

scenes.dialogue: Third, the plaint is insufficiently stamped, and the stamp paper is not supplied in time. Fourth, the suit appears, from the statement in the plaint, to be barred by law.
Fifth, the plaint is not filed in duplicate. Sixth, the plaintiff fails to comply with Rule Nine. For valuation and stamp defects, the plaintiff first gets time to correct them.
scenes.shown: Fifth, the plaint is not filed in duplicate. Sixth, the plaintiff fails to comply with Rule 9. For valuation and stamp defects, the plaintiff first gets time to correct them.

scenes.dialogue: How closely must a court read a plaint? In T Arivandandam versus T V Satyapal, the Supreme Court said the plaint must receive a meaningful reading.
scenes.shown: How closely must a court read a plaint? In T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, the Supreme Court said the plaint must receive a meaningful reading.

scenes.dialogue: Clever drafting cannot manufacture a cause of action where none exists. So the court must look past the drafting to the substance.
Picture a plaint full of impressive allegations, but missing the material facts that create a right to relief. Drafting a plaint? Plead those material facts.
But the court must identify a ground under Rule Eleven. It cannot reject a plaint merely because the case looks difficult. Seeking rejection? Name the ground.
scenes.shown: But the court must identify a ground under Rule 11. It cannot reject a plaint merely because the case looks difficult. Seeking rejection? Name the ground.

scenes.dialogue: What may the court read? In Dahiben versus Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali, the answer is the plaint as a whole, with the documents it relies on.
scenes.shown: What may the court read? In Dahiben v. Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali, the answer is the plaint as a whole, with the documents it relies on.

scenes.dialogue: Acting for the defendant? Your competing version of the facts does not decide a Rule Eleven application.
scenes.shown: Acting for the defendant? Your competing version of the facts does not decide a Rule 11 application.

scenes.dialogue: In Dahiben, a sale deed was challenged years later. The Court upheld the rejection. The suit was time barred, and lacked a sustainable cause of action.
scenes.shown: In Dahiben, a sale deed was challenged years later. The Court upheld the rejection. The suit was time-barred, and lacked a sustainable cause of action.

scenes.dialogue: Practice point: check the pleaded dates and documents carefully. Limitation supports rejection only when the bar is apparent from the plaint.
Acting for the plaintiff? Disputed facts cannot simply be resolved against your client at this stage.
The flip side is return. A properly pleaded claim may still be filed in the wrong court.
Under Rule Ten, the plaint is returned for presentation to the court where the suit should have been instituted. Return is about the forum, not the merits.
scenes.shown: Under Rule 10, the plaint is returned for presentation to the court where the suit should have been instituted. Return is about the forum, not the merits.

scenes.dialogue: The judge endorses the plaint with the dates of presentation and return, the presenter's name, and brief reasons for returning it.
Where its conditions apply, Rule Ten A can fix an appearance date in the proper court.
scenes.shown: Where its conditions apply, Rule 10A can fix an appearance date in the proper court.

scenes.dialogue: What happens in the proper court? In O N G C versus Modern Construction, the Supreme Court said the returned plaint is treated as a fresh institution.
scenes.shown: What happens in the proper court? In ONGC v. Modern Construction, the Supreme Court said the returned plaint is treated as a fresh institution.

scenes.dialogue: The trial proceeds afresh. It does not continue the earlier suit, so limitation matters.
Section Fourteen of the Limitation Act may exclude the time spent pursuing the case in a court without jurisdiction. But that protection must be established.
scenes.shown: Section 14 of the Limitation Act may exclude the time spent pursuing the case in a court without jurisdiction. But that protection must be established.

scenes.dialogue: Return does not preserve the original filing date, so never assume it protects your client.
Is a return just a transfer? No. The three judge bench in E X L Careers versus Frankfinn Aviation Services confirmed it.
scenes.shown: Is a return just a transfer? No. The three-judge bench in EXL Careers v. Frankfinn Aviation Services confirmed it.

scenes.dialogue: After a return under Rules Ten and Ten A, the proceedings must begin afresh.
scenes.shown: After a return under Rules 10 and 10A, the proceedings must begin afresh.

scenes.dialogue: Rule Ten A simplifies appearance and service. It does not turn a return into a transfer that keeps the earlier trial stage.
scenes.shown: Rule 10A simplifies appearance and service. It does not turn a return into a transfer that keeps the earlier trial stage.

scenes.dialogue: One qualification. In E X L itself, the Supreme Court used its constitutional powers on exceptional facts, and left the High Court's order undisturbed.
scenes.shown: One qualification. In EXL itself, the Supreme Court used its constitutional powers on exceptional facts, and left the High Court's order undisturbed.

scenes.dialogue: That relief does not change the general rule. Cite E X L for the rule, not for its result.
scenes.shown: That relief does not change the general rule. Cite EXL for the rule, not for its result.

scenes.dialogue: Rejected? That rejection is deemed a decree under Section Two, sub section Two. So it ordinarily attracts a first appeal under Section Ninety Six.
scenes.shown: Rejected? That rejection is deemed a decree under Section 2(2). So it ordinarily attracts a first appeal under Section 96.

scenes.dialogue: An order returning a plaint is appealable under Order Forty Three, Rule One, clause A, except where the Rule Ten A procedure was followed.
scenes.shown: An order returning a plaint is appealable under Order XLIII Rule 1(a), except where the Rule 10A procedure was followed.

scenes.dialogue: Rejection does not, by itself, bar a fresh plaint on the same cause of action. Rule Thirteen says so.
scenes.shown: Rejection does not, by itself, bar a fresh plaint on the same cause of action. Rule 13 says so.

scenes.dialogue: But a fresh plaint must still overcome limitation and the legal defect. Refiling a barred claim does not remove the bar.
Test yourself with two plaints. The first pleads a recoverable debt, but the chosen court lacks territorial jurisdiction. Think return, under Rule Ten.
scenes.shown: Test yourself with two plaints. The first pleads a recoverable debt, but the chosen court lacks territorial jurisdiction. Think return, under Rule 10.

scenes.dialogue: The second plaint, read with its own documents, discloses no cause of action. Think rejection, under Rule Eleven.
scenes.shown: The second plaint, read with its own documents, discloses no cause of action. Think rejection, under Rule 11.

scenes.dialogue: Before drafting or opposing either application, check these four things: the forum, the material facts, the documents relied on, and limitation.
Return sends the plaint to the proper court. Rejection follows a specified statutory ground. Get it right: that distinction decides the next step in the entire case.
